name: Tarafa ibn al-Abd
bio: Tarafa ibn al-Abd was a pre-Islamic poet of Bakr ibn Wa'il, born in the desert of eastern Arabia. He travelled in Najd. His Mu'allaqa moves from Khawla's abandoned camp to his riding camel and his troubled place among his own people. Al-Zirikli relates that King Amr ibn Hind first admitted him to his company, then sent him to the governor carrying the written order for his own death. He was killed young at Hajar, around 60 years before the Hijra (564 CE).
